topic: Changes in Materials When Heated, Cooled, or Mixed
key_concepts: Matter changes when exposed to different temperatures or mixed with other materials.
Heating increases temperature; cooling decreases temperature.
Heated materials can change in size, shape, form, and texture.
Heating can change solids to liquids (melting).
Cooling can change liquids back to solids.
Butter, chocolate, crayons, and candle wax melt when heated and harden when cooled.
Hot water dissolves solids like sugar and coffee faster than cold water.
Heating chocolate, butter, and crayons is a physical change.
Solid materials can be mixed with other solid materials.
Some mixtures show one or two phases of matter.
